title: Choose the visual world for totp-auth
question: The roll assigned Seed Packet Catalog. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Seed Packet Catalog
options.lineage: mid-century seed-company packets and catalog plates
options.thesis: A TOTP secret is a seed; every entry is a printed packet and the code is the sow-by date.
options.viewport: Dark leaf-green shell with a left rail, search on top, and a list of packet rows; each row has a colour band, issuer in condensed caps, a large grouped code and a days-to-maturity style countdown bar.
options.risk: Cute if the packet colours spread past the issuer band.

raised.raise: Entries sit in fixed-size cells that reflow in whole cells, never squeezed, so each packet stays whole at every width.
Every state is a printed mark at one hairline weight: expired is struck through, focus is bracketed, disabled is run through.
Only the packet last copied from takes full colour; idle packets print in single ink so the active code is the loudest thing on screen.

options.label: Swiss Station Timetable
options.lineage: 1950s Swiss railway timetables and platform clocks
options.thesis: Codes set like departures in a timetable, with a station-clock sweep hand that pauses at the rotation.
options.viewport: Light shell, top bar with search, rows in strict columns: issuer, account, code, and a small sweep clock whose hand stops at 30 seconds before restarting.
options.risk: Also the grounded direction most runs in this category land on, and it sits close to a generic Swiss-minimal look.

options.label: Split-Flap Board
options.thesis: Rotation is the product: when the 30 seconds end, every code cascades to its new value flap by flap.
options.viewport: Dark shell, rows of fixed character cells, each code a row of six flaps, amber lamp on the entry in its last five seconds.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: rotation maps to the cascade and the cells keep digits unmistakable. It holds product clarity and loses audience identification, since a personal user has no tie to stations.
options.risk: Reads as a novelty widget if the cascade fires on every tick instead of only at rotation.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.thesis: Soft cards on a warm ground, with the one saturated colour reserved for things you can press.
options.viewport: Warm tinted ground, white cards, each with a big tappable code and a copy button; a bottom bar on narrow widths.
options.case: Holds product clarity at full strength and reads as a real authenticator. It loses on distinctiveness, since neighbours already ship it.
options.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: A night-use vault: codes in chalk on navy, urgency drawn as a red ring, like the object under the eye.
options.viewport: Navy shell, entries as ranked rows with magnitude dots by recent use; the entry nearest expiry is ringed in red.
options.case: Holds audience identification for late-night logins and the dark scene; loses clarity because dot size reads as ornament until learned.
options.risk: Ornament outweighs the task if the constellation layer is more than faint.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.case: Loses both axes: a mascot per account is a joke the product cannot carry, and it reads as a toy for a security tool.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference Setting
options.case: Loses both axes: two dense text columns fight a list of codes, and a personal user does not read reference books.
options.kept: States printed as marks at one hairline weight.

options.label: Factory Catalog Sleeve
options.case: Loses both axes: names replaced by coded colour strips would make the issuer unreadable at the moment of login.
options.kept: Only the active item is decoded to full colour.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: An authenticator app as people already know it, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: White shell, list of entries with large code and a thin countdown ring, tap to copy.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
